title: fix(objectql): an item registered through the registry path is served with its package's `_packageVersion`
body:
Fixes #22689

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`_packageVersion` is declared on the spec's protection envelope (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`: "Owning package version."). The metadata plugin's artifact loader stamps it through `applyProtection(item, { packageId, packageVersion })`. The registry load path, `ObjectQL.registerApp(manifest)` into `SchemaRegistry.registerItem` / `registerObject`, called `applyProtection(item, { packageId })` and stamped the id alone. The comment above that call said both paths "produce identical lock state". They did not: `GET /api/v1/meta/app` served a registry-registered app with `_packageId` and no `_packageVersion`, so a console waiting on an upgrade could not tell the new app from the old one a stale kernel still serves (the upgrade case behind objectstack-ai/objectui#12087).

Premise checked on `origin/main` `61bea242`: both `applyProtection` sites in `registry.ts` passed `{ packageId }` only. Measured before the change: the served app had `_packageVersion` undefined (ablation A below is that reading).

## How the version reaches the registry

The caller that holds a package's manifest stamps each item **before** handing it to the registry, with the artifact loader's own call, `applyProtection(item, { packageId, packageVersion })`. `applyProtection` writes a key only while it is unset, so the registry's own id-only stamp leaves the caller's envelope as stamped. **The registry's public signatures are unchanged** (`SchemaRegistry.registerItem`, `registerObject` and `registerApp`, signature and JSDoc as on `main`), and both of its `applyProtection` calls still pass `{ packageId }` alone. No version table, no second manifest list, no lookup in the registry's installed-package record (which would stamp a tenant row merely bound to a package with a version it was never shipped at), no implicit context and no new export.

- `ObjectQL.registerApp(manifest)`, the private `registerPlugin` and the private `registerMetadataCollections` stamp through two module-local helpers in `engine.ts`:
  - `stampPackage` stamps apps, collection items, view items, seed data and extensions in place, as the registry already mutates them on `main`;
  - `stampObjectPackage` stamps a shallow **copy** of each authored object definition, so a payload registered twice (the ADR-0130 D7 pin) is never mutated. The test pins this: "the authored object definition is left unstamped".
  - Both do nothing when `manifest.version` is absent. A nested plugin's items carry the parent's version, as they carry its id.
- `ObjectQLPlugin`'s residual registration (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects`, landed from `main` in PR #22701 after dispatch) stamps a shallow copy of each residual object with `unclaimedTopLevel(stack)`'s `(ownerId, ownerVersion)` before `registerObject`, the pair the metadata door stamps the residual with.

**`Clause-②: no`, by measurement:** the declaration closure that `@objectstack/objectql`'s `.` and `./core` entries reach is byte-identical to `origin/main` (`e5899a67d6`): 3 of 3 closure files and 6 of 6 dist declarations. A determinism control (head versus a rebuilt head) is identical. A positive control carrying round 0's trailing parameter differs in 12 places, so the instrument sees a widening.

## Callers that have no version, and stamp the id alone

`applyProtection` never invents a version, so these are unchanged:

- `SchemaRegistry.registerKind` and `registerItem('plugin', manifest, 'id')`: no package id at all.
- `ObjectQLPlugin.loadMetadataFromService`, `ingestReloadedObjects` and the per-object refresh, and `MetadataFacade.register`: they pass the item's own `_packageId`. An item that came through the artifact loader already carries `_packageVersion`, and `applyProtection` keeps it.
- The metadata-protocol stored-row paths (hydration, write-through, rollback): `registerItem` with no package id, or `registerObject` of a `_provenance: 'org'` row under its binding. These are tenant-authored, not shipped by a package version.
- plugin-security's built-ins (`registerBuiltinPositions` / `registerBuiltinCapabilities`): the plugin's own id.
- `ObjectQL.registerObject(schema, packageId, namespace)`: the public proxy, unchanged.

The comment above `registerItem`'s `applyProtection` call now says this instead of "identical lock state".

## Files outside the claimed surface

The claim named `registry.ts`, the registry's callers inside `packages/objectql/src/`, tests there, and one changeset. Two more files changed. Both are test pins that asserted the asymmetry this card closes, and both went red with the change:

- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts`: "the registry copy carries no `scope` (and no `_packageVersion`)". It now expects the registry copy to carry `_packageVersion: '3.0.0'`, the version the door copy carries.
- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-security-registrar.test.ts` (the control case): `expect(got.capability[0]._packageVersion).toBeUndefined()`. It now expects `'2.0.0'`. The comment says `scope` is the one key that still tells the raw copy from the door's.

## Tests (round 1, head `73fc84cbed`)

- New `packages/objectql/src/registry-package-version-stamp.test.ts`:
  - an app and an object registered through `ObjectQL.registerApp` are served with `_packageVersion` through the real list door;
  - an upgrade (1.0.0, then 1.1.0) is served with the new version;
  - a nested plugin's object and a collection item carry the owning version;
  - an id-only caller stamps the id alone;
  - the authored object definition is left unstamped;
  - CONTROL: the artifact loader door (`MetadataPlugin._parseAndRegisterArtifact`, unchanged) serves an identical envelope.
- `manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`: the residual object carries the stack's version (`1.0.0`).
- `engine.test.ts`: one manifest gained `version: '1.2.0'`, and its pin asserts `objectContaining({ name, _packageId, _packageVersion: '1.2.0' })`. The other call-shape pins are `main`'s.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql` vitest (`--project local`, two foreground shards): 397 files and 7,773 tests passed, 0 failed. Typecheck exit 0, with the test layer's pinned debt held.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: typecheck exit 0. Vitest in two shards: 348 files, 0 failed.
- **Round 0's CI red** on `7539a404` (`Test Core (6/6)`, `artifact-load-path.test.ts`'s ADR-0130 D7 pin) was caused by this card's first caller-side stamp mutating the authored object in place. It is fixed by stamping a copy, and the D7 test is green and unchanged.

## Reverse verification

Both legs used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from the committed head, with each restore proven (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty):

- **A:** `stampPackage`'s stamp removed. Predicted and observed: 5 red (the new file's app, upgrade, nested and control cases, plus the `engine.test.ts` version pin); the id-only, residual and D7 cases green.
- **B:** the residual stamp removed. Predicted and observed: only the residual case red.

## Gates

All 70 families that `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives for this diff ran at `73fc84cbed`, and each exited 0. `--ran`: 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was first recorded as PREREQUISITE NOT MET in a recreated worktree and re-run after a full build, exit 0. A narrowed `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 8 changed `.ts` files reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. Repo-wide lint is CI's. CI on `73fc84cbed`: 31 success, 3 skipped.

## Line budget

+213 / -34 across 9 files, against a suggested 150:
- code: `engine.ts` +49/-18, `plugin.ts` +14/-4, `registry.ts` +10/-3 (comments only);
- tests: the new file +112, and +15/-9 elsewhere;
- changeset: +13.

The new test file carries the cross-door control and the copy pin.

## Acceptance notes

- `SchemaRegistry.updatePackageManifest` (the in-memory half of `PATCH /packages/:id`) can change a package record's `version` without restamping the items already registered. They keep the version they were installed with. This is a read-only inference; it was not exercised.
- The objectui follow-up objectstack-ai/objectui#12098 consumes this field. The rebuild-pending read is cloud's (objectstack-ai/cloud#2760) and is not in this PR.
